label: has no relationship to
type: an explicit, docs-stated assertion that two systems/concepts that share surface similarity (or even a product) are deliberately unrelated - minted specifically for Sync Gateway's docs stating its own channel/role/user model and its reused server-RBAC model 'have no relationship'
note: Low recurrence but promoted for its semantic significance - this is the sharpest piece of evidence for the round's headline finding (one product, two disjoint access-control systems). Also a candidate relation for resolving the still-open search-admin/fts-admin docs-issue, IF a page is ever found stating those are unrelated (none has been, so far).
qualifying_note_round_28: The standing sgw:user hasNoRelationshipTo sgw:rbac-user triple is QUALIFIED, not retracted, by round 28's rest_api_admin.json. That record's own evidence: 'Create a new user session' (Admin API, POST /{db}/_session) - which mints a Public-API session cookie on behalf of a named sgw:user - is itself gated by the Server-RBAC roles role:sync-gateway-configurator/role:sync-gateway-app ('Required Sync Gateway RBAC roles: Sync Gateway Architect, Sync Gateway Application'), and creating/managing sgw:role and sgw:user objects (Public-API, channel-grant objects) likewise requires holding one of those same Server RBAC roles via the Admin API (see requiresServerRole relations on sgw:role and sgw:database in rest_api_admin.json). So: the ORIGINAL claim holds exactly as stated for AUTHENTICATION - the two identity systems never share a login, and a Sync Gateway user/role is never itself a Server RBAC principal, or vice versa. What round 28 adds is that the relationship is asymmetric at the ADMINISTRATION layer: a caller holding the right Server RBAC role can create, edit and impersonate (via session creation) objects in the channel-based system, while the reverse (a channel-based sgw:user reaching into Server RBAC) is asserted nowhere. This is a real refinement worth carrying forward in any future reading of this relation, not a correction of round 27's original quote-licensed claim.
